'''Kanbara Shrine''' (神原神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|kamochou|ja|加茂町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamochō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11398866}}, {{ill|Unnan|en|Unnan|qid=Q877935|lt=Unnan City}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}. It is known for the discovery of a {{ill|triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} with the inscription "Jingchu 3rd Year" during the excavation of an ancient Kofun on its former grounds.

== Deities ==

The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}}, {{ill|Iwatsutsunoo|ja|磐筒男命}}, and Iwatsutsume-no-Mikoto. 

The earliest record appears in the {{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記}}, under the entry for Kanbara-go in Ōhara District. Initially, it is believed that only Ōkuninushi was worshipped {{why|date=2022}}. However, the 1708 document ''Kanbara Shrine Engi'' compiled by Hirozawa Urushihiro, the priest of {{ill|Mito Tenmangū|ja|三刀屋天満宮}}, lists the deities as Iwatsutsunoo and Iwatsutsume-no-Mikoto.

== History ==

The ''{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記}}'' refers to the shrine as "Kanbara Shrine," stating that it belonged to the {{ill|Department of Divinities|ca|Jingi-kan|es|Jingikan|fa|اداره امور شینتو|fr|Jingi-kan|id|Jingikan|ja|神祇官|ko|신기관|nl|Jingi-kan|pt|Jingi-kan|ru|Дзингикан|simple|Department of Divinities|tr|Jingi-kan|uk|Дзінґікан|vi|Thần kỳ quan|zh|神祇官|qid=Q2264720|lt=Department of Divinities}}. The record also describes Kanbara-go as "the place where the treasures of the Heavenly Grand deity (Ōkuninushi) are stored." 

The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} lists the shrine as "Kanbara Shrine." Various names have appeared over time, including "Kanbara Matsui Daimyōjin" (1611) on a ridgepole inscription, "Kanbara Shrine Matsui Daimyōjin" in the ''Kanbara Shrine Engi,'' and "Shinpo Myōjin" in the 1717 ''Un'yōshi.''

In December 1871, the shrine was Ranked as a village shrine. The current structure was relocated in 1972 due to flood control work on the {{ill|Akagawa River (Unnan City)|ja|赤川 (雲南市)}} within the {{ill|Hii River|en|Hii River|qid=Q11500714|lt=Hii River system}}.

== Kanbara Shrine Kofun ==

[[File:kambarajinjakofunsekisitsu.JPG|thumb|right|Reconstructed stone chamber of Kanbara Shrine Kofun]]
[[File:神原神社古墳出土 三角縁神獣鏡 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|Replica of a triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror<br />{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|National Museum of Japanese History|en|National Museum of Japanese History|qid=Q3330690|lt=National Museum of Japanese History}}.}}]]

The shrine's former grounds were situated atop an ancient Kofun ([[kofun]]). The mound is a {{ill|square tumulus|ja|方墳}}, estimated to measure 29 meters by 25 meters and approximately 5 meters in height. It is among the oldest kofun in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, dating to the early period.

During flood control work in 1972, the shrine was moved approximately 50 meters southwest, and the kofun was excavated. Artifacts found in the [[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|Pit-style stone chamber]] included a "Jingchu 3rd Year" (239 CE) {{ill|triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}}, identified as a relic of the {{ill|Three Kingdoms period|ja|三国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Kingdoms period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11354714}}. These artifacts are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}, housed at the {{ill|Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo|en|Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo|qid=Q4802099|lt=Shimane Prefectural Ancient Izumo History Museum}}. The stone chamber has been reconstructed east of the relocated shrine and is open for public viewing.

== Festivals ==

The annual festival held on November 9 includes a lion dance, designated as an {{ill|Q11476462|ja|島根県指定文化財一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11476462}}. Rituals are also conducted during the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6364021}} period.
